requirements.requirement: Forward inventory-tagged log messages from node2 to node1 and persist them at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: A synthetic inventory message from node2 was received at the required path on node1. Final observations show valid filtering/forwarding configurations, active and enabled rsyslog services, an established TCP connection, and the collector listening on port 514.

requirements.requirement: Keep log persistence and forwarding operational after node1 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, changed boot identity, recovered its listener and existing log data, and then received a fresh inventory event from node2.

requirements.requirement: Keep log forwarding operational after node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node2 had a healthy pre-restart forwarding connection, acknowledged the restart, changed boot identity, recovered rsyslog and its TCP connection, and sent a fresh inventory event that was persisted on node1 alongside the pre-restart event.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Direct message-delivery tests establish the initial flow and persistence, while sequential restart transitions on both managed nodes demonstrate boot-identity changes, service recovery, reconnection, preservation of earlier data, and successful delivery of fresh post-restart inventory messages. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and agrees with the fixed lifecycle boot observations.
limitations: Application behavior was tested using logger with the inventory program tag rather than evidence from a distinct inventory application process; this directly exercises the configured routing path but does not independently characterize that application's own logging behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The persistent directory, rsyslog configurations, restricted firewall rule, and service restarts directly implemented the requested flow; synthetic log writes and both restarts established bounded final evidence. The timed-out node2 status query did not show an additional mutation. Lifecycle observations show no failed services, package damage, or unrelated temporary residue after execution.
